cannot_reverse: the registered E1 and E2 verdicts. This analysis characterises how much of E1's positive certificate and E2's negative census survives changing one assumption at a time.

concentration_inequality.note: tighter L1 bound for finite alphabets

concentration_inequality.eps: empirical simultaneous quantile of ||phat-p||_1 under parametric multinomial resampling
concentration_inequality.note: NOT a bound; shows how conservative the bounds are

delta_lower_solver: exact LP over the expanded vertex set
E1_axes.jackknife: leave one cell out at the cohort registration, 28 refits

E2_axes.note: the registered pair is [0.15, 0.35]; a near-collision could be hiding just outside the registered extreme classes

predictions_registered_in_advance.S1: The cohort registration stays non-vacuous under every inequality and every eta. If it does not, E1's positive result is an artefact of the chosen bound.
predictions_registered_in_advance.S2: The unit registration stays vacuous under every inequality and every eta.
predictions_registered_in_advance.S3: The slack bound and the exact LP agree to within 0.01 at every registration where the LP is solvable.
predictions_registered_in_advance.S4: No leave-one-cell-out refit at the cohort registration turns the certificate vacuous.
predictions_registered_in_advance.S5: The minimum cross-grade pairwise TV stays above 0.05 at every threshold pair, i.e. E2's 'no natural near-collision' does not depend on where the buffer was cut.

prohibited: Selecting the inequality, eta, or threshold pair that gives the most favourable certificate and reporting only that.
Using the bootstrap radius as if it were a bound; it is reported only to show how much the bounds give away.
Letting any outcome here change the E1 or E2 registration.
